officialTitle: Talazoparib in Patients with Advanced Breast Cancer and a Germline BRCA Mutation
setting: Advanced breast cancer, germline BRCA1/2 mutation

design.blinding: Open-label; PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Of the 431 patients who underwent randomization, 287 were assigned to receive talazoparib and 144 were assigned to receive standard therapy.
design.notes: 2:1 randomisation. Comparator: single-agent physician's choice (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine).

clinicalQuestion: Is talazoparib superior to physician's choice single-agent chemotherapy in advanced breast cancer with a germline BRCA1/2 mutation?

pico.population: Advanced breast cancer with a germline BRCA1/2 mutation
pico.comparator: Single-agent physician's choice (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine)
pico.outcomes: Primary: PFS by BICR. Secondary: OS, ORR, safety, patient-reported outcomes

arms.label: Talazoparib
arms.doseSourceQuote: assigned, in a 2:1 ratio, to receive talazoparib (1 mg once daily) or standard single-agent therapy of the physician's choice (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine in continuous 21-day cycles)

arms.label: Physician's choice chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine (physician's choice), continuous 21-day cycles

publications.title: Talazoparib in Patients with Advanced Breast Cancer and a Germline BRCA Mutation.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Median progression-free survival was significantly longer in the talazoparib group than in the standard-therapy group (8.6 months vs. 5.6 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41 to 0.71; P<0.001).

outcomes.analysisLabel: Interim OS analysis (57% of projected events)
outcomes.sourceQuote: The interim median hazard ratio for death was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.55 to 1.06; P=0.11 [57% of projected events]).
The objective response rate was higher in the talazoparib group than in the standard-therapy group (62.6% vs. 27.2%; odds ratio, 5.0; 95% CI, 2.9 to 8.8; P<0.001).

safety.sourceQuote: Hematologic grade 3-4 adverse events (primarily anemia) occurred in 55% of the patients who received talazoparib and in 38% of the patients who received standard therapy
nonhematologic grade 3 adverse events occurred in 32% and 38% of the patients, respectively

strengths: Randomised phase III trial with PFS by blinded independent central review
limitations: Interim OS not significant at 57% of projected events

clinicalImplications.text: Supports talazoparib as an oral PARP inhibitor option for advanced breast cancer with a germline BRCA1/2 mutation, with PFS and patient-reported outcome benefits over single-agent chemotherapy.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Talazoparib's main toxicity is haematologic (largely anaemia) — monitor blood counts closely in the first cycles.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 30110579. Final OS analysis not ingested.
